candidate_relations.reason: Lymphoma is the compatible tumor family for a ventral cervical mass in a llama but omits the required T-cell immunophenotype.
Soft-tissue sarcoma is a different lineage from T-cell lymphoma and is not supported by any histologic pattern in this record.
Thyroglossal duct cyst is a congenital cystic remnant, whereas ultrasonography showed a solid heterogeneous encapsulated mass without a tract.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma would arise in thyroid parenchyma; the mass had no tracheal or esophageal communication and no thyroid-specific markers.
A granuloma could fit mild warmth and neutrophilia, but that inflammatory mass conflicts with the reference T-cell lymphoma.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma is an epithelial thyroid neoplasm, not a subcutaneous encapsulated cervical lymphoma.
Neoplasm is a parent of T-cell lymphoma and does not specify lymphoid lineage or T-cell phenotype.
Fluctuance, warmth, and neutrophilia raise abscess, which is a competing infectious mass rather than T-cell lymphoma.
Neoplasia likewise names a growth process but not the T-cell lymphoma required by the reference.
No trauma is described, and a mildly warm, painful, neutrophilic mass is not a simple hematoma.
Lipoma is typically cool, painless, and homogeneous, unlike this warm fluctuant mass causing inspiratory noise.
An abscessated lymph node is an infectious node process that conflicts with T-cell lymphoma as the final object.
Streptococcal abscess assigns a bacterial etiology unsupported by culture and incompatible with T-cell lymphoma.
Thyroid carcinoma is the wrong organ and lineage for a mid-cervical mass with no visceral communication on endoscopy.
Myxoma is a benign mesenchymal tumor not suggested by the heterogeneous encapsulated cervical mass or the CBC.
Branchial cleft cyst is a developmental lateral neck cyst, not an encapsulated heterogeneous mass attributed to T-cell lymphoma.
The llama remained bright with a one-week mass effect, unlike invasive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma destroying local structures.
Follicular thyroid carcinoma is an epithelial thyroid tumor unsupported by any thyroid-origin imaging.
Squamous cell carcinoma is a different malignant lineage from T-cell lymphoma, and overlying skin was normal.
Thyroid adenocarcinoma similarly names glandular thyroid cancer rather than a T-cell lymphoid neoplasm.

case_quality_flags: The record describes a ventral cervical mass and CBC only; no histopathology or immunophenotype confirming T-cell lymphoma is provided.
